title: Fix: encode all non-alphanumeric chars in Claude Code project paths
body: Claude Code keys its session store at `~/.claude/projects/<bucket>/`, where `<bucket>` is the project path with every non-alphanumeric character replaced by -. ctxmv replaced only /. So a project like `/Users/me/public_html/site.example.com` was written to `-Users-me-public_html-site.example.com` while Claude reads `-Users-me-public-html-site-example-com`. Migration reported success, but Claude never saw the imported session.

The `ubi` backend in mise is deprecated upstream in favor of the `github` backend, which covers the same functionality with fewer dependencies. See:

title: Fix Claude Code resume: emit resume-contract-compliant JSONL
body:
## Problem

Migrating a session into Claude Code produced a file that **failed to resume in the TUI** — `claude --resume <id>` printed `Failed to resume session <id>`, even from the correct project directory.

This was hidden because earlier verification used headless `claude --resume -p`, which is **lenient** and loads the same file fine. The interactive TUI enforces a stricter contract. (The previously merged path-alias work, #16, did not fix this — it addressed a different, non-causal hypothesis.)

## Root cause & evidence

Using a pty-driven TUI resume harness (`script -q /dev/null claude --resume …`, broken=FAIL / known-good=OK calibrated), I bisected the exact requirements. The migrated JSONL violated three:

1. **First line was `progress`.** The TUI rejects a session whose first line is `progress`. (A real session's first line is a conversation entry; it has no `progress` lines at all.)
2. **Entries lacked `cwd`/`version`/`gitBranch`/`isSidechain` and a `parentUuid` chain.**
3. **Assistant messages lacked `message.model`** (any non-empty value suffices).

## Fix (ctxmv-only — no schema/AgentSessions change)

- Write the `ctxmv_migration` meta as a **trailing** `progress` line. Dedup reads the whole file (`readMigrationMeta` iterates all lines), so re-migration detection is unaffected; the first line is now the first conversation entry.
- Populate `cwd`/`version`/`gitBranch`/`isSidechain`/`parentUuid` on each entry — all already exist on `ClaudeCodeEntry`.
- Set `message.model` on assistant entries, falling back to a sentinel when the source has none.

Verified end-to-end: a freshly migrated session resumes successfully in the real TUI.

## Also

- Regression test asserting the emitted JSONL shape (no leading progress, trailing meta, required entry fields, model on assistant, parentUuid chain).
- Corrects the stale `CLAUDE.md` gotcha that claimed the first line *must* be `progress` — the opposite is true.

title: Fix: write migrated Claude Code sessions to symlink-aliased project buckets
body:
## Problem

Claude Code resolves `--resume` strictly against the current working directory — it only looks in `~/.claude/projects/<encoded cwd>/` (verified: resuming from an unrelated cwd returns `No conversation found`).

When a project lives under a **symlinked parent** (e.g. `~/workspace -> /Volumes/Disk/workspace`), two paths refer to the same directory:
- **physical** `/Volumes/Disk/workspace/proj` — what Codex/Cursor session metadata records, and what `getcwd` returns (symlinks resolved)
- **logical** `~/workspace/proj` — what the user actually `cd`s into

These encode to **different** project buckets (`-Volumes-Disk-...` vs `-Users-me-...`). ctxmv only wrote the physical bucket, so `claude --resume` failed when the user ran it from the logical path — even though the session migrated correctly.

## Fix

Add `ClaudeProjectAliasResolver`. It recovers the alias for free from the shell: `PWD` is the *logical* invocation dir (symlinks preserved), while `getcwd`/`FileManager.currentDirectoryPath` is *physical* (resolved). When `PWD` canonicalizes to the same path as the physical bucket but differs as a string, it is a genuine alias.

`ClaudeCodeMigrator` now:
- writes the session into **every** aliased bucket, and
- dedups across **all** buckets (so a re-migration doesn't write one alias while throwing `alreadyMigrated` on another).

The canonicalization guard means an unrelated invocation directory never receives a stray session — without it, no alias bucket is written and behavior is unchanged.

## Tests

- `ClaudeProjectAliasResolverTests` — alias returned for a real symlink; nothing returned when `PWD` equals physical / is unrelated / is absent.
- `ClaudeCodeMigratorTests` — session lands in both buckets under a symlink; only the physical bucket otherwise.
- Full suite: 92 tests pass.

## Note

This is the path half of a two-part fix. The other half (Codex `response_item` user turns being dropped on migration) lives in [AgentSessions#5](https://github.com/Ryu0118/AgentSessions/pull/5); once that ships in a release, ctxmv's dependency will be bumped separately.

title: feat: match sessions by opening prompt text
body:
## Summary

- Bump AgentSessions to 0.4.0 which adds `SessionSummary.initialPrompt` (first meaningful user message)
- `ShowRunner.matchingSummary` now falls back to matching against `initialPrompt` when ID and suffix lookups both fail

## Motivation

`ctxmv migrate 'prompt' --to claude-code --from codex` was
reporting "Session not found" because only session ID and 8-char suffix were checked.
Codex's own `resume` command uses the opening prompt as the session identifier, so users naturally
pass that same string to ctxmv.

## Test plan

- [ ] `swift test` — 86 tests pass
- [ ] `ctxmv migrate '<opening prompt>' --to claude-code --from codex` resolves the correct session
